equivalence_vectors.name: Set arrays sort by UTF-8 bytes of JCS serialization, not UTF-16 code units
equivalence_vectors.why: U+FF5E (EF BD 9E) sorts before U+1F600 (F0 9F 98 80) in UTF-8 byte order; a UTF-16 sort reverses them and produces a different digest.

pin_ordering_vector.description: definition_pins[] is ordered by ref_kind, then by the JCS bytes of reference (whose members sort by name, so collection_id precedes publisher_domain), both compared as UTF-8 bytes. The input order below is deliberately shuffled and includes same-kind pins whose domain order disagrees with their id order and a non-ASCII id.

non_ijson_vectors.description: A string containing a lone surrogate is not I-JSON, so the entry has no JCS form. A verifier treats the definition as unresolvable (changed).
An integer a double cannot hold exactly is not I-JSON; two different published numbers would collide. A verifier treats the definition as unresolvable (changed).
A duplicate member name is not I-JSON and parsers disagree on which value wins, so two verifiers could compute different digests. A verifier treats the definition as unresolvable (changed).
A number that overflows an IEEE 754 double is not I-JSON. A verifier treats the definition as unresolvable (changed).
Nesting deeper than 64 levels is rejected so a hostile document cannot exhaust a verifier. A verifier treats the definition as unresolvable (changed).
A literal backslash followed by the text ud800 is not a lone surrogate and resolves.
A member literally named __proto__ is valid and stays in the preimage.
The largest exactly representable integer and a valid surrogate pair are I-JSON and resolve.

collection_mutation_vector.description: The pinned collection is mutated after the proposal is committed. commercial_terms is untouched, so terms_digest still verifies, but the pin no longer verifies.
